intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Bhutan is a place of virgin forests, crystal rivers, snow capped peaks, and tropical environs. This Buddhist Monarchy is one of the least traveled destinations in the world, yet it hosts some of the best opportunities for hiking, biking, rafting, and cultural immersion in the Himalayas. This one week itinerary combines aspects of Bhutanese history, culture and food paired with activities tailored to fit your thirst for adventure.

groups.title: Enter the Dragon Kingdom
prose: Approaching Bhutan is like nothing else. The Himalayas fill the horizon. You encounter your first Bhutanese hosts on the plane because their national airlines are the only ones who fly in and out of the country. The snow-capped peaks disappear as you descend into the Paro Valley and arrive at the only international airport in the nation. Paro is 7,200 feet (2200m) above sea level and is home to Paro Airport, several famous Dzongs, the national museum, and the famous Tiger's Nest but it only serves as the port of entry and a brief stop for a quick meal before we head to Thimphu, the nation's capital. Don't worry! You will experience the best of Paro on the back end of this journey.

The drive from Paro to Thimphu is approximately one hour. After checking in at your hotel, get some rest and take it easy to acclimatize to the capital's elevation of 7,656 feet (2320m). Bhutan has some of the most unique cuisine in the Himalayas so join the group for an evening meal together along with an in depth orientation from your guides.

groups.title: A Day in the Capital
prose: As the civic and cultural heart of Bhutan, a day in the capital allows for an introduction to many important aspects of Bhutan's national identity. You can visit one of the temple complexes, known as dzongs, a cultural museum, and the Takin Preserve. These three places allow foster an understanding of Bhutan's Buddhist culture, rich history, and extensive biodiversity. It will be an active day of walking but at a pace that still allows for acclimatization. There are many other things as well but we suggest saving some of these a the return through the capital.

groups.title: Punakha via Dochula Pass
prose: Punakha is an adventurer's dream: hiking, biking, rafting, fishing, and fortresses to be explored or myths to be entertained. Reaching Punakha via the Dochula pass is a treasured experience in itself, with views of Bhutan's great peaks from the top of the pass.

Punakha's riverside temple and government complex is one of the most impressive in the country. Built in 1637, it was host to the coronation of the current monarchy's first king in 1907 and served as the capital until 1955. Take a wanderers approach to this architectural marvel and learn from your guide as he explains the multifunctional importance of Punakha Dzong.
Visit the Dzong and enjoy a night near Punakha before starting your customized days of adventure.

groups.title: Punakha & Khotokha Adventure Opportunities
prose: With options to choose from, this is one place where your itinerary may be customized to accommodate for tailored adventure selections. Choose from multiple activities or go further with one selection. Mountain biking, river rafting, hiking, and deeper cultural exploration are accessible in this region.
Raft the Mo Chu for a relaxed float trip or the Po Chu for faster currents and bigger rapids.
Go mountain biking in Khotokha's serene valley setting.
Birding in the region's RAMSAR site can provide opportunities to see the Black Neck Crane (seasonal).
Hike to one of the region's many cultural or spiritual landmarks, combining physical and cultural opportunities.

groups.title: Multi-day Hiking
prose: Now that you are adjusted to the altitude, choose one of Bhutan's famous trails for a longer hike/trek. This could be the Trans-Bhutan Trail (TBT). Hike several sections to put together a multi-day adventure with a specialty trekking crew that is hand picked to give you an incredible experience with rich Bhutanese personalities. This can be done in multiple areas of central or western Bhutan, depending on what suits your fitness goals as well as your overall itinerary choices.

groups.title: Paro and the Tiger's Nest
prose: We will make our way back to where it began, Paro. On arrival, stretch your legs on the streets of Paro, try a local coffee shop to experience Bhutan's home grown coffee, and shop for that special item to serve as a connection to your memories in Bhutan.

The Tiger's Nest is one of the most iconic destinations in Bhutan and the only way to get there is on foot. A day hike to the Tiger's Nest is the best way to conclude any trip to Bhutan. It combines activity, culture, and the nature of Bhutan's mountainside environment. And have you heard of the hot stone baths? Reward yourself after the hike with one of those!

Local farmhouses in the region can date back 7 or more generations and one of these is always recommended as a residence for your time in Paro. The homegrown ingredients will fill your plates and the hospitality of the family will entice you to return. The Bhutanese hot stone baths that are common in these homesteads are a highlight for any trip to Bhutan.

groups.title: Day of Departure
prose: All good things must come to an end but you are welcome to come again! Your guide will transfer you to the airport for your departure on this day.

included: Guide Services - professional, English speaking guides as well as English speaking activity guides
Activities as listed in your itinerary.
Accommodations: Our preferred packages include 3–4 star locations in Bhutan. Farmhouse stays are not rated in the same way as hotels, but are highlighted experiences by all our guests.
Meals: All meals in Bhutan are provided in the tour package.
Domestic transportation: All ground transportation is provided by private vehicle.
excluded: Alcohol: We strongly encourage minimizing or eliminating alcohol while acclimatizing. Should you choose to drink alcohol when appropriate, you may do so but must pay your alcohol tab at the close of the meal.
Tips: It is customary to tip all guides. We will provide information about the tipping culture in Bhutan so you can make informed decisions regarding when to tip and how much to tip.
Clothing and Equipment: We do not provide your gear but do have a packing list to help you prepare. We are happy to answer any questions you have and make recommendations if you need assistance.
